Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 8, verse 1:

Surat al-Anfal [Madaniyya (Medinan), except from verse 30 to the end of verse 36, which are Makkan. Its verses number 75 or 77. It was revealed after al-Baqara.]

When the Muslims disagreed over the spoils of Badr, the young men said: "They are ours, because we engaged in the fighting." The elders said: "We were a reserve force for you under the banners, and if you had been routed, you would have retreated to us. So do not monopolize them." Then the following was revealed:

﴿They ask you﴾, O Muhammad, ﴿about the spoils (al-anfal)﴾, the booty: to whom do they belong? ﴿Say﴾, say to them: ﴿The spoils belong to God﴾, He places them wherever He wills, ﴿and the Messenger﴾ divides them by the command of God. So he (ﷺ) divided them among them equally. Narrated by al-Hakim in al-Mustadrak. ﴿So fear God and set right what is between you﴾, that is, reform the reality of your relations with one another through affection and abandoning dispute. ﴿And obey God and His Messenger, if you are truly believers﴾ in truth.

﴿Truly the believers﴾ are those who are perfect in faith, ﴿those whose hearts tremble when God is mentioned﴾, meaning His threat, ﴿feared﴾, ﴿their hearts﴾, ﴿and when His verses are recited to them, they increase them in faith﴾, meaning in affirmation, ﴿and in their Lord they put their trust﴾, meaning they rely on Him and not on anything else.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 8, verse 3:

﴿Those who establish the prayer﴾ bring it with its requirements (ḥuqūq). ﴿And from what We have provided them﴾ given them, ﴿they spend﴾ in obedience to Allah.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 8, verse 4:

﴿Those﴾ who are described by what was mentioned ﴿are the believers truly﴾, in truth, without doubt. ﴿For them are ranks﴾, stations in Paradise ﴿with their Lord, and forgiveness and a generous provision﴾, in Paradise.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 8, verse 5:

﴿As your Lord brought you forth from your house in truth﴾ — this is related to "brought forth" (akhraja). ﴿And indeed a party of the believers were averse﴾ — to the going forth. The clause is a circumstantial clause (hal) from the kaf in "akhrajaka" (you). And "kama" (as) is the predicate of an omitted subject, meaning: this condition in their aversion to it is like your bringing forth in the condition of their aversion; and it was good for them, so likewise also. The reason was that Abu Sufyan arrived with a caravan from al-Sham, so the Prophet ﷺ and his companions went out to seize it as booty. Quraysh learned of this, so Abu Jahl and the fighters of Makkah went out to defend it, and they were the army of relief (al-nafir). Abu Sufyan took the caravan by the coastal road and escaped, and it was said to Abu Jahl, "Turn back," but he refused and proceeded to Badr. The Prophet ﷺ consulted his companions and said, "Indeed Allah has promised me one of the two groups." They agreed with him to fight the army of relief, but some of them disliked that and said, "We did not prepare for it," as the Most High said:

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 8, verse 6:

﴿They dispute with you concerning the truth﴾ — i.e., the fighting — ﴿after it has become clear﴾ — i.e., after it has become manifest to them — ﴿as if they were being driven toward death while they look on﴾ — i.e., looking at it plainly (ʿiyānan), in their aversion to it.

And [remember] when Allah promised you one of the two groups, that it would be yours, and you wished that the group without strength would be yours. That is, the group without might and weapons, which was the caravan (al-'ir), because of the small number of its men and its lack of reinforcement, unlike the army (al-nafir). But Allah intended to establish the truth by His words, that is, by making Islam prevail, which was His earlier word, and to cut off the last remnant of the disbelievers through total annihilation. So He commanded you to fight the army (al-nafir).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 8, verse 8:

﴿That He might establish the truth and nullify falsehood﴾ — yamhaq (He would destroy) ﴿the falsehood﴾, which is disbelief, ﴿even though the criminals﴾, the polytheists, ﴿dislike it﴾.

Remember when you sought help from your Lord, and He answered you: "I will reinforce you with a thousand of the angels, following one another." (Tafsir of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti, on surah 8, verse 9)

[Translation of the commentary:]

﴿Remember﴾ when you sought aid (تَسْتَغِيثُونَ) from your Lord (تَطْلُبُونَ مِنهُ الغَوْث), asking Him for help (بِالنَّصْرِ) against them. ﴿So He answered you: that I﴾ (أيْ بِأَنِّي), i.e., that I will be ﴿your reinforcer﴾ (مُمِدّكُمْ), ﴿your helper﴾ (مُعِينكُمْ), ﴿with a thousand of the angels, following one another﴾ (مُتَتابِعِينَ), one of them coming after another (يُرْدِف بَعْضهمْ بَعْضًا). He had promised them this first (وعَدَهُمْ بِها أوَّلًا), then it became three thousand (ثُمَّ صارَتْ ثَلاثَة آلاف), then five thousand, as in Surat Al ʿImran (ثُمَّ خَمْسَة كَما فِي آل عِمْران). It is also read as ﴿bi-ʾalf﴾ (بِآلُف) in the form of ʾaflus (كَأَفْلُس), a plural (جَمْع).
﴿And Allah did not make it﴾ i.e., the reinforcement (al-imdad).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 8, verse 11:

﴿When He covers you with drowsiness as a security from Him﴾, (a security) from what had befallen you of fear; ﴿and sends down upon you water from the sky to purify you thereby﴾ from the minor and major ritual impurities; ﴿and to remove from you the defilement of Satan﴾, his whispering into you that, had you been upon the truth, you would not have been thirsty and in a state of ritual impurity while the polytheists had the water; ﴿and to strengthen your hearts﴾, (to bind upon them) by certainty and patience; ﴿and make firm thereby your feet﴾, so that they would not sink into the sand.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 8, verse 12:

﴿When your Lord revealed to the angels: "Indeed I am with you, so strengthen those who have believed. I will cast terror into the hearts of those who disbelieved, so strike [them] above the necks and strike every fingertip of them."﴾

(Those whom He sent down to the Muslims) — (that) is, "that I am with you" — by way of aid and victory. (So strengthen those who have believed) — by means of assistance and good tidings. (I will cast terror) — fear — (into the hearts of those who disbelieved.) (So strike above the necks) — that is, the heads. (And strike every fingertip of them) — that is, the extremities of the two hands and the two feet. Thus a man would intend to strike the neck of an unbeliever, and it would fall before his sword reached him. And the Prophet (ﷺ) threw at them a handful of pebbles, and there was no polytheist who did not have some of it enter his eyes, so they were routed.
﴿That﴾, the punishment that befalls them, ﴿because they opposed﴾ (defied) ﴿Allah and His Messenger. And whoever opposes Allah and His Messenger, indeed Allah is severe in punishment﴾ for him.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn on 8:14:

﴿That﴾ (is) the punishment, ﴿so taste it﴾, O disbelievers, in this world; ﴿and that for the disbelievers﴾ (is the punishment) in the Hereafter.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 8, verse 15:

﴿O you who have believed, when you meet those who disbelieve advancing [in ranks], do not turn your backs to them [in flight].﴾ Meaning: gathered together, as if, because of their great number, they were creeping forward [zahf].

﴿So do not turn your backs to them﴾ fleeing in defeat.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 8, verse 16:

﴿Whoever turns his back to them on that day﴾ – i.e., the day of their encounter – ﴿unless he is swerving﴾ – turning aside – ﴿for battle﴾ – by making them think he is fleeing as a stratagem, while he intends to return to the attack – ﴿or joining﴾ – gathering together – ﴿a company﴾ – a group of the Muslims, seeking their support – ﴿then he has incurred﴾ – returned with – ﴿wrath from Allah, and his abode is Hell, and wretched is the destination﴾ – the place of return – it. And this is specific to the case where the disbelievers do not exceed twice the number [of the Muslims].

Tafsir al-Jalalayn (al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti) on Surah 8, verse 17:

﴿So you did not kill them﴾ at Badr by your own strength, ﴿but it was God who killed them﴾ by His help to you, ﴿and you did not throw when you threw﴾, O Muhammad, at the eyes of the people, ﴿but it was God who threw﴾ by delivering that to them, He did it in order to humble the disbelievers, ﴿and that He might test the believers with a fair trial from Him﴾, a fair gift, which is the booty, ﴿indeed God is All-Hearing﴾ of their words, ﴿All-Knowing﴾ of their states.
﴿That﴾, the *iblāʾ* (a great favour or trial from God) is *ḥaqq* (a due, a truth), and ﴿that Allah is the one who weakens﴾ (*muḍʿif*, the one who diminishes the strength of)

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 8, verse 19:

﴿If you seek a decision﴾ O disbelievers, if you seek victory, i.e., judgment, when Abu Jahl among you said: "O Allah, whichever of us was more severing of kinship and came with what we do not recognize, then destroy him this morning," i.e., destroy him. ﴿Then there has certainly come to you the decision﴾, the judgment, by the destruction of the one who is such, and he is Abu Jahl and those killed with him, rather than the Prophet (ﷺ) and the believers. ﴿And if you cease﴾ from disbelief and war, ﴿then it is better for you. And if you return﴾ to fighting the Prophet (ﷺ), ﴿We will return﴾ to his support against you. ﴿And your company will not avail you at all﴾, i.e., will not repel from you, ﴿even if it is plentiful. And indeed, Allah is with the believers﴾. The particle inna is read with a kasra, as a resumed sentence, and with a fatha, on the basis of an assumed lam (la-anna).
O you who believe, obey Allah and His Messenger, and do not turn away from him (tu'ridu, "turn away") by opposing his command, while you hear (the Qur'an and the admonition).
﴿And do not be like those who say, "We hear," while they do not hear.﴾ [They are] hearing of reflection and admonition. They are the hypocrites or the polytheists.

The commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 8, verse 22:

﴿Indeed, the worst of living creatures in the sight of Allah are the deaf﴾ to hearing the truth, ﴿and the dumb﴾ from speaking it, ﴿who do not reason﴾, those who do not understand it.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 8, verse 23:

﴿Had Allah known any good in them﴾ (i.e., goodness, meaning readiness to accept the truth when heard) ﴿He would have made them hear﴾ (i.e., hearing with understanding). ﴿And had He made them hear﴾ (hypothetically, while He knows there is no good in them) ﴿they would have turned away﴾ from it ﴿while being averse﴾ to accepting it, out of obstinacy and denial.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 8, verse 24:

﴿O you who have believed, respond to Allah and to the Messenger﴾ with obedience, ﴿when he calls you to that which gives you life﴾ from the matter of the religion, because it is the cause of eternal life. ﴿And know that Allah intervenes between a man and his heart﴾ so that he cannot believe or disbelieve except by His will, ﴿and that to Him you will be gathered﴾ so that He will recompense you for your deeds.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 8, verse 25:

﴿And guard yourselves against a trial﴾ which, if it befalls you, ﴿will not afflict only those among you who have done wrong﴾ specifically, but will encompass them and others as well. Guarding against it is by denouncing what necessitates it of wrongdoing. ﴿And know that Allah is severe in punishment﴾ for whoever opposes Him.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 8, verse 26:

﴿And remember when you were few and oppressed in the land﴾ the land of Makkah, ﴿fearing that the people would snatch you away﴾ that the disbelievers would seize you quickly. ﴿So He sheltered you﴾ in al-Madinah, ﴿and strengthened you﴾ made you strong ﴿with His help﴾ on the Day of Badr, with the angels, ﴿and provided for you of the good things﴾ the spoils of war, ﴿that you might be grateful﴾ for His blessings.

Revealed concerning Abu Lubabah Marwan ibn Abd al-Mundhir, whom the Prophet (ﷺ) had sent to the Banu Qurayzah so that they would come down to submit to his judgment. They consulted him, and he gestured to them that it was slaughter (al-dhabh), for their families and property were among them. ﴿O you who have believed, do not betray Allah and the Messenger or betray your trusts﴾, that which you have been entrusted with, of the religion and other than it.

﴿And know that your wealth and your children are only a trial﴾ for you, diverting you from the matters of the Hereafter, ﴿and that with Allah is a great reward﴾, so do not forfeit it by attending to wealth and children, and by betrayal for their sake. And it was revealed concerning his repentance:

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 8, verse 29:

﴿O you who have believed, if you fear Allah⁠ — by turning back to Him and other means — ﴾ ﴿He will grant you a criterion⁠﴾ between you and what you fear, so that you are saved, ﴿and will remove from you your misdeeds and forgive you⁠﴾ your sins.

﴿And﴾ remember, Muhammad, ﴿when those who disbelieved plotted against you﴾, while they had gathered for consultation about your affair in Dar al-Nadwa (the council house of the Quraysh) ﴿to restrain you﴾, meaning to bind you and imprison you, ﴿or kill you﴾, all of them together, as the killing of one man, ﴿or expel you﴾ from Mecca. ﴿They plot﴾ against you, ﴿and Allah plots﴾ against them, by arranging your affair, in that He revealed to you what they had planned and commanded you to leave. ﴿And Allah is the best of planners﴾, the most knowing of them about it.

When Our verses are recited to them, they say: "We have heard. If we wished, we could say the like of this." This was said by al-Nadr ibn al-Harith, because he used to go to al-Hira on trade and buy books of the stories of the non-Arabs (al-a'ajim), and he would relate them to the people of Makkah. "This is nothing but" — i.e., the Qur'an is nothing but — "fables" (asatir), i.e., falsehoods.

﴿And when they said, "O Allah, if this is indeed the truth from You"﴾ [the one that Muhammad recites] ﴿"then rain down on us stones from the sky, or bring us a painful punishment"﴾ painful because of their denial. This was said by al-Nadr and others, mockingly, and to give the impression that they were certain of it, while being firmly convinced of its falsehood.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 8, verse 33:

﴿And Allah would not punish them﴾ for what they asked [for], ﴿while you are among them﴾, because when punishment descends it encompasses all, and a community is never punished until its prophet and the believers have left it. ﴿And Allah would not punish them while they seek forgiveness﴾, where they say in their circumambulation: "Forgiveness, [O Allah], forgiveness." It was also said that they are the believers among them who were oppressed, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Had they been separated, We would have punished those who disbelieved among them with a painful punishment﴾.

﴿And what is it with them that Allah should not punish them﴾ with the sword after your departure [from Mecca], and [after the departure] of the oppressed [believers who remained there]. According to the first opinion, it [this verse] is abrogating (*nasikhah*, i.e. *naskh*, abrogation) what precedes it. Allah did punish them at Badr and elsewhere. ﴿While they bar﴾ prevent the Prophet (ﷺ) and the Muslims ﴿from al-Masjid al-Haram﴾ from circumambulating it. ﴿And they were not its guardians﴾ as they claimed. ﴿Its guardians are only the God-fearing [*in*]﴾ here *in* is *ma*, meaning "not": ﴿its guardians are only the God-fearing, but most of them do not know﴾ that they have no guardianship over it.

﴿Their prayer at the House was nothing but whistling﴾ (ṣafīran) ﴿and clapping﴾ (taṣfīqan). That is, they made that the place of their prayer, in place of the prayer they had been commanded to perform. ﴿So taste the punishment﴾ at Badr.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 8, verse 36:

﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve spend their wealth﴾ in the war against the Prophet (ﷺ), ﴿in order to averted [people] from the way of Allah. So they will spend it, but it will then be a regret upon them﴾ in the final outcome of the matter, ﴿[a source of] regret﴾ [for them] because it is lost and because what they intended is lost too, ﴿and then they will be overcome﴾ in this world, ﴿and those who disbelieve﴾ among them ﴿will be gathered to Hellfire﴾ in the Hereafter, ﴿they will be driven﴾ [there], i.e., led on.

﴿لِيَمِيزَ﴾ is related to تَكُونُ (*takūnu*, "will be"), read with the light (التَّخْفِيف, *takhfīf*) or the heavy (التَّشْدِيد, *tashdīd*) pronunciation. That is, He separates ﴿اللَّه الخَبِيث﴾ the disbeliever ﴿مِن الطَّيِّب﴾ from the believer. ﴿ويَجْعَل الخَبِيث بَعْضه عَلى بَعْض فَيَرْكُمهُ جَمِيعًا﴾ He places the evil, some of it upon some, and so He piles it up, gathering it all together, heaped one part upon another.

Say to those who disbelieve, such as Abu Sufyan and his companions: if they desist from disbelief and from fighting the Prophet (ﷺ), what has passed will be forgiven them of their deeds; but if they return to fighting him, then the way of the earlier peoples has already passed (i.e., Our practice concerning them, of destruction), and so We will do to them.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 8, verse 39:

﴿And fight them until there is no more fitnah﴾ (shirk) occurring, ﴿and religion is entirely for Allah﴾ alone, and nothing else is worshipped. ﴿But if they desist﴾ from disbelief, ﴿then indeed Allah is Seeing of what they do﴾, so He will recompense them for it.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 8, verse 40:

﴿And if they turn away﴾ from faith, ﴿then know that Allah is your Protector (mawlakum)﴾ your Helper and the One who manages your affairs, ﴿an excellent Protector﴾ He is, ﴿and an excellent Helper﴾, i.e., the Helper for you.

﴿And know that whatever you take as spoils﴾, meaning what you seize by force from the disbelievers, ﴿of anything, then for Allah is its one-fifth﴾ (khums), ﴿He commands concerning it what He wills﴾, ﴿and for the Messenger and for the near of kin﴾, meaning the relatives of the Prophet ﷺ from Banu Hashim and Banu al-Muttalib, ﴿and the orphans﴾, meaning the children of the Muslims whose fathers have died and who are poor, ﴿and the needy﴾, meaning those in want among the Muslims, ﴿and the wayfarer﴾, meaning the one stranded during his journey among the Muslims. That is, it belongs to the Prophet ﷺ and to these four categories, according to the way he used to divide it: each of them receives one-fifth of the fifth, and the remaining four-fifths belong to those who gained the spoils (al-ghanimun). ﴿If you have believed in Allah﴾, then know this. ﴿And what﴾ is conjoined to "in Allah," ﴿We sent down upon Our servant﴾, Muhammad ﷺ, ﴿of the angels and the signs﴾, ﴿on the day of the Criterion﴾ (al-Furqan), meaning the day of Badr, which distinguished truth from falsehood, ﴿the day the two hosts met﴾, the Muslims and the disbelievers. ﴿And Allah is over all things competent﴾, and by that power He gave you victory despite your small number and their large number.

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 8, verse 42:

﴿When﴾ is a substitute for "the day" in ﴿you were﴾ (staying) ﴿on the nearer bank﴾, meaning the side closer to Madinah. ﴿Al-'udwa﴾ is pronounced with a ḍamma or a kasra on the ʿayn, and means the side or bank of the valley. ﴿And they were on the farther bank﴾, meaning the side farther from it. ﴿And the caravan﴾, meaning the merchandise, was in a place ﴿below you﴾, on the side nearer the sea. ﴿Even if you had made an appointment﴾, you and the enemy, to fight, ﴿you would have differed about the appointment. But﴾ he gathered you without any appointment ﴿so that Allah might accomplish a matter that was to be done﴾, which was in His knowledge, namely the victory of Islam and the destruction of disbelief. ﴿So that he who would perish might perish﴾, meaning who would disbelieve, ﴿upon clear evidence﴾, meaning after a manifest proof had been established against him, which was the victory of the believers despite their small number over the large army. ﴿And he who would live﴾, meaning who would believe,

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 8, verse 43:

﴿When Allah showed them to you in your dream as few⦆ — that is, in your sleep (manam-ka, "your sleep"). ﴿And had He shown them to you as many, you would have lost heart﴾ — you would have been cowardly, ﴿and you would have disputed﴾ — and differed, ﴿concerning the matter﴾ — the matter of fighting, ﴿but Allah saved you﴾ — but Allah saved you from that. ﴿Indeed, He is Knowing of what is in the breasts﴾ — of what is in the hearts.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 8, verse 44:

﴿And when He showed them to you, O believers, when you met [them], as few in your eyes﴾ about seventy, or a hundred, while they were a thousand, ﴿so that you might advance upon them;﴾ ﴿and He made you seem few in their eyes﴾ so that they would advance and not turn back from fighting you. This was before the fighting joined; but when it joined, He showed them to them as twice their number, as is mentioned in Surat Al ʿImran. ﴿That Allah might accomplish a matter that was to be done;﴾ ﴿and to Allah all matters are returned﴾ i.e., they will end up with Him.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 8, verse 45:

﴿O you who have believed, when you meet a company [of disbelievers]﴾ a disbelieving group ﴿then stand firm﴾ for fighting them and do not flee ﴿and remember Allah much﴾ call upon Him for victory ﴿that you may be successful﴾ that you may win.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 8, verse 46:

﴿And obey Allah and His Messenger, and do not dispute, lest you lose courage and your strength depart⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠ — and be patient. Indeed, Allah is with the patient.﴾

Note: the translation above was incomplete; the full rendering follows.

﴿And obey Allah and His Messenger, and do not dispute﴾ [i.e., do not differ among yourselves], ﴿lest you lose courage﴾ [i.e., become cowardly], ﴿and your strength depart﴾ [i.e., your power and your dynasty], ﴿and be patient. Indeed, Allah is with the patient﴾ [i.e., with help and support].

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 8, verse 47:

﴿And do not be like those who went forth from their homes﴾ to prevent others [from the path of Allah], and did not return after their rescue ﴿insolently and to be seen by people﴾, when they said: "We will not return until we have drunk wine, slaughtered camels, and had singing girls played for us at Badr, so that the people will hear of it." ﴿And they bar⁠﴾ people ﴿from the way of Allah. And Allah is Encompassing of what they do﴾, with the ya' and the ta' (both readings: yaʿmalūna and taʿmalūna), ﴿encompassing﴾ in knowledge, so He will recompense them for it.

And [mention] when Satan (al-Shaytan, i.e. Iblis) made their deeds appear attractive to them, by encouraging them to meet the Muslims, when they feared going out against their enemies, the Banu Bakr. And he said [to them]: "No one among the people will overcome you today, and I am a protector for you" — from Kinanah. He had come to them in the form of Suraqah ibn Malik, the chief of that region.

﴿Then when the two groups sighted each other﴾, i.e. met, the Muslim and the disbelieving groups, and he saw the angels with his hand in the hand of al-Harith ibn Hisham, ﴿he turned back on his heels﴾, i.e. retreated, fleeing, ﴿and said﴾ when they said to him, "Will you abandon us in this situation?": ﴿"Indeed I am free of you"﴾, i.e. of your protection, ﴿"Indeed I see what you do not see"﴾, i.e. the angels, ﴿"Indeed I fear Allah"﴾, i.e. that He will destroy me.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 8, verse 49:

﴿When the hypocrites and those in whose hearts is a disease say﴾ (a disease): weakness of belief. ﴿"These have been deluded in their religion"﴾ i.e., the Muslims, in that they went out, despite their small number, to fight the large host, supposing that they would be given victory because of it. Allah the Exalted said in reply to them: ﴿"And whoever puts his trust in Allah"﴾ believes in Him and relies upon Him, ﴿"then indeed Allah is Mighty"﴾ overpowering in His command, ﴿"Wise"﴾ in His creation.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 8, verse 50:

﴿And if you could see﴾ O Muhammad, ﴿when the angels take the souls of those who disbelieve﴾ (read with the ya' and with the ta', i.e. yatawaffa or tatawaffa), ﴿striking their faces and their backs﴾ (this is a circumstantial clause, ḥāl), ﴿with iron maces﴾ (maqāmi' min ḥadīd), ﴿and [saying to them]﴾ ﴿"Taste the punishment of the burning"﴾, i.e. the Fire. The answer to "law" (if) is: "you would see a tremendous matter."

"That" (the punishment) "is because of what your hands have sent forth" (ﷺ... no) — here is the translation:

"That" [refers to the punishment] "because of what your hands have sent forth." He expressed it with "hands" rather than other [body parts] because most actions are carried out with them. "And that Allah is not ever unjust [ﷻ] to the servants" — i.e., not one who does injustice — so that He would punish them without a sin.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 8, verse 52:

﴿Kada'b﴾ (like the custom/habit) of ﴿the folk of Pharaoh and those before them, who disbelieved in the signs of Allah, so Allah seized them﴾ with punishment ﴿for their sins﴾. The clause "who disbelieved" and what follows it explain what precedes it. ﴿Indeed Allah is Mighty﴾ over whatever He wills.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 8, verse 53:

﴿That﴾ i.e., the punishment of the disbelievers, ﴿is because﴾ i.e., due to the fact that ﴿Allah never changes a blessing He has bestowed upon a people﴾ — changing it into a curse — ﴿until they change what is in themselves﴾ — they alter their blessing into disbelief, like the disbelievers of Makkah who [changed] feeding them after hunger and securing them after fear, and sending the Prophet ﷺ to them, into disbelief, obstructing the way of Allah, and fighting the believers.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 8, verse 54:

﴿As was the custom of the people of Pharaoh and those before them: they denied the signs of their Lord, so We destroyed them for their sins, and We drowned the people of Pharaoh﴾ — his people, along with him — ﴿and all﴾ of the nations that denied.
And it was revealed concerning Quraydhah: ﴿Indeed, the worst of living creatures in the sight of Allah are those who disbelieve, so they will not believe.﴾

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 8, verse 56:

﴿The ones with whom you made a covenant﴾ [that they would not help the polytheists] ﴿then they break their covenant every time﴾ that they make it ﴿and they do not fear﴾ Allah in their treachery.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 8, verse 57:

﴿Fa-immā﴾: in it there is the assimilation (idghām) of the nūn of in (the conditional particle) into the extra mā. ﴿Tathqafannahum﴾: you find them. ﴿Fī al-ḥarb fa-sharrid﴾: in war, then disperse/put to flight. ﴿Bihim man khalfahum﴾: by them, those behind them, from among the fighters, by making an example of them and by punishment. ﴿La'allahum﴾: that is, those who are behind them. ﴿Yadhdhakkarūn﴾: they will take warning from them.

﴿And if you fear treachery﴾ from a people [who] made a covenant with you (عاهَدُوك), ﴿treachery﴾ in a covenant, by a sign that becomes apparent to you, ﴿then throw back﴾ i.e. cast off their covenant ﴿to them, on equal terms﴾, a *ḥāl* (circumstantial clause, here, the grammatical state of the subject), meaning: you and they being equal in knowledge of the breaking of the covenant, by informing them of it, lest they accuse you of treachery.

It was revealed concerning those who escaped on the day of Badr: "And let not those who disbelieve suppose, O Muhammad, that they have outstripped" Allah, meaning they have escaped Him, "indeed they cannot escape." That is, they cannot get away from Him. In another reading, with the yā' (ي) at the beginning of the verb, the first object is omitted, meaning "themselves" (anfusahum). In another reading, with the hamzah of "innahum" vocalized with a fatḥah, it is according to the estimate of the lām (i.e., "because they cannot escape").

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 8, verse 60:

﴿And prepare against them﴾ for fighting them ﴿whatever you can of strength﴾ He (ﷺ) said, "It is archery." Narrated by Muslim. ﴿and of steeds of war (ribat al-khayl)﴾ a verbal noun meaning keeping them in the way of Allah ﴿to strike terror﴾ frighten ﴿into the enemy of Allah and your enemy﴾ i.e., the disbelievers of Makkah ﴿and others besides them﴾ i.e., others than them, and they are the hypocrites or the Jews ﴿whom you do not know; Allah knows them. And whatever you spend in the way of Allah will be repaid to you﴾ its reward ﴿and you will not be wronged﴾ you will not be deprived of any of it.

﴿And if they incline﴾ (māllū), meaning they lean, ﴿to peace﴾ (al-silm, read with either a kasra or a fatha on the sīn), meaning reconciliation, ﴿then incline to it﴾, meaning make a covenant with them. Ibn ʿAbbās said: this ruling is abrogated (mansūkh, from naskh, "abrogation") by the verse of the sword (āyat al-sayf). Mujāhid said: it is specific to the People of the Book (ahl al-kitāb), since it was revealed concerning Banū Qurayẓa. ﴿And rely upon Allah﴾, meaning trust in Him. ﴿Indeed He is the All-Hearing﴾ of speech, ﴿the All-Knowing﴾ of deeds.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 8, verse 62:

﴿And if they intend to deceive you﴾ with the peace agreement, so that they may prepare themselves against you, ﴿then indeed, Allah is sufficient for you﴾ (sufficient for you), ﴿He is the One who supported you with His help and with the believers﴾.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 8, verse 63:

﴿And He joined﴾ (i.e., He gathered) ﴿their hearts together﴾ after the enmities (al-ihan) ﴿Even if you had spent all that is in the earth, you could not have joined their hearts together, but Allah joined them together﴾ by His power ﴿Indeed, He is Mighty﴾ (ghalib) over His affair ﴿Wise﴾ nothing escapes His wisdom.
O Prophet, Allah is sufficient for you, and so are those believers who follow you.

O Prophet, urge the believers to fight (lit. "incite"/"rouse") against the disbelievers. If there are twenty of you who are steadfast, they will overcome two hundred of them. And if there are a hundred of you, they will overcome a thousand of those who disbelieve, because they are a people who do not comprehend.

This is a report in the form of a command: that twenty of you should fight two hundred, and a hundred should stand firm against a thousand. Then it was abrogated (naskh) when they increased in number, by His saying:

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 8, verse 66:

﴿Now Allah has lightened your burden, and He knows that there is weakness in you﴾ — read with a ḍammah or a fatḥah on the ḍād — concerning fighting ten times your number. ﴿So if there are among you a hundred steadfast, they will overcome two hundred﴾ — read with the yā' or the tā' (yakun / takun) — of them. ﴿And if there are among you a thousand, they will overcome two thousand by the permission of Allah﴾ — by His will. This is a statement in the form of a report but carrying the meaning of a command, i.e., "Fight your two-fold and stand firm against them." ﴿And Allah is with the steadfast﴾ — by His help.

It was revealed when they took ransom from the captives of Badr. ﴿It is not for a Prophet to have captives﴾ (read with the taa' or the yaa', i.e., "takūna" or "yakūna") ﴿until he has inflicted slaughter upon the land﴾ (yubāligh fī qatl al-kuffār, i.e., he exerts himself thoroughly in killing the disbelievers) ﴿you desire﴾ O believers ﴿the goods of this world﴾ (ḥuṭāmuhā, its fleeting wealth) by taking ransom ﴿but Allah desires﴾ for you ﴿the Hereafter﴾ (i.e., its reward) by their killing ﴿and Allah is Mighty and Wise﴾. And this verse has been abrogated (mansūkh) by His saying: ﴿Then either grace afterwards or ransom﴾.

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 8, verse 68:

﴿Had there not been a decree from Allah that had already preceded﴾ by making the spoils of war (al-ghana'im) and the captives lawful for you, ﴿you would have been touched, for what you took﴾ from the ransom.

O Prophet, say to those prisoners who are in your hands (and in another reading, "the captives," al-Usara) : ﴿If Allah knows any good in your hearts﴾ meaning faith and sincerity, ﴿He will give you better than what has been taken from you﴾ meaning the ransom, by multiplying it for you in this world and rewarding you in the Hereafter, ﴿and forgive you﴾ your sins.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 8, verse 71:

﴿And if they intend treachery against you﴾, i.e., the captives, ﴿then they have already betrayed Allah before﴾, before Badr, through disbelief, ﴿so He gave you power over them﴾ at Badr, by killing and taking them captive. So let them expect the same if they return. ﴿And Allah is Knowing﴾ of His creation, ﴿Wise﴾ in His doing.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 8, verse 72:

﴿Indeed, those who believed and emigrated and strove with their wealth and their lives in the cause of Allah﴾ — and they are the Muhajirun (the emigrants) — ﴿and those who sheltered and helped﴾ the Prophet (ﷺ) — and they are the Ansar (the helpers) — ﴿those are allies of one another﴾ in support and inheritance. ﴿As for those who believed but did not emigrate, you have no obligation of guardianship toward them﴾ — the word wilayatihim may be read with a kasra or a fatha on the waw — ﴿at all﴾ — so there is no inheritance between you and them, and they have no share in the spoils — ﴿until they emigrate﴾. This ruling has been abrogated (mansukh) by the last part of the surah. ﴿And if they seek your help in religion, then it is incumbent upon you to help them﴾ against the disbelievers, ﴿except against a people between you and whom there is a covenant﴾, meaning a treaty; so do not help them, lest you break your covenant with them.

﴿And those who disbelieve, some of them are allies of others﴾, in support and inheritance. ﴿So there is no inheritance between you and them﴾. ﴿Unless you do it﴾, that is, supporting the Muslims and suppressing the disbelievers, ﴿there will be fitnah (civil strife and trial) in the land and great corruption﴾, through the strength of disbelief and the weakness of Islam.
﴿Those who believed, emigrated, and strove in the cause of God, and those who gave shelter and helped: these are the true believers. For them is forgiveness and a generous provision﴾ in Paradise.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 8, verse 75:

﴿And those who believed after [the earlier ones]﴾, i.e., after the foremost (al-sabiqun) to faith and emigration, ﴿and emigrated and strove alongside you﴾, ﴿those are of you﴾, O emigrants and Helpers (al-Ansar), ﴿and those of blood relationship﴾, the kindred, ﴿are nearer to one another﴾ in inheritance, by way of inheritance (al-tawarruth) through faith and emigration mentioned in the previous verse, ﴿in the Book of Allah﴾, the Preserved Tablet (al-lawh al-mahfuz), ﴿indeed Allah is Knowing of all things﴾, and from this is the wisdom of inheritance (al-mirath).
